corrected_value.authors: Schneider, D., Bayliss, A. P., Becker, S. I., & Dux, P. E.
corrected_value.title: Eye movements reveal sustained implicit processing of others’ mental states.

decisions.quote: As an additional test for order effects, Study 2 (n = 82) was designed to replicate the Schneider et al. (2012) paradigm in a single session to rule out more stringent multitest or order effects. The findings were comparable with the nonreplication described above (see Fig. 3).
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state files exist for this work. Studies 1 (n = 108) and 2 (n = 82) empirically retest the anticipatory-looking false-belief finding of Schneider, Bayliss, Becker, & Dux (2012) ('Eye movements reveal sustained implicit processing of others’ mental states.', Journal of Experimental Psychology: General, 141, 433–438; no DOI printed in source) using original stimuli and procedures, comparing the 2 x 2 Belief x Location ANOVA and planned contrasts at the no-object and object locations against the original findings. The sole shipped row (input_row_index 1877) is Southgate, Senju, & Csibra (2007; 10.1111/j.1467-9280.2007.01944.x), an independent study by different authors in a different journal using a different paradigm, and Schneider et al. (2012) is also distinct from all sibling targets (Surian & Geraci, 2012; Low & Watts, 2013; Senju et al., 2009), so report equivalence does not apply.
